newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai foreign borrowing near critical-central bank.
newsitem.headline: Thai foreign borrowing near critical-central bank.

text.p: The level of foreign borrowing by the Thai private and public sector is reaching a critical point and steps must be taken to control such loans, a senior central bank official said on Tuesday.

Central bank economist Bandid Nijathaworn told a news conference that the Bank of Thailand (BOT) would be formulating a policy to control the direction of the rising foreign borrowing. He did not, however, state when such a policy would be implemented.
According to central bank figures, national foreign borrowing totalled US$82.6 billion last year compared with $37.9 billion in 1991.
Private sector borrowing (including borrowing by commercial banks) amounted to $41 billion in 1995 against $14.6 billion in 1991, the data showed.
"There must be implementaton of a policy to direct and control foreign borrowing of the private sector because the amount has reached a critical point," Bandid said.
Foreign borrowing through foreign loans and to a lesser extent via the issue of bonds has soared over the past five years because of prohibitively high domestic interest rates, analysts said.
